clue.text: Witness implicating Socialist leader in parliament is extremely sleazy

indicators.note: a leader stands at the front, so only the opening letter of the word before it is kept
one piece is placed in the middle of the other, which then surrounds it

blocks.note: to witness something is to see it
a diet is a formal legislative assembly, as in Japan or historically Germany
the first letter of Socialist

explanation.surface: A witness gives evidence that drags a socialist party leader into a parliamentary sleaze scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: A diet is the name for some national parliaments, such as Japan's. 'Implicating' only strings the witness onto the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Seedy means shabby and disreputable, and the superlative form describes the most disreputable or sordid of all.

clue.text: Column in Standard with hurtful contents

indicators.note: the word given as contents sits inside the other word, which holds it

blocks.note: par is the standard or normal level, as in golf
ill can mean harmful or hurtful, as in ill effects

explanation.surface: A newspaper column in the Evening Standard full of hurtful remarks.
explanation.walkthrough: The Standard is a London newspaper, so 'Column in Standard' reads like journalism; PAR holds ILL to give P(ILL)AR.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillar is an upright supporting post in a building, the architectural sense of column.

clue.text: Man perhaps taken for a ride after losing case

indicators.note: the case is the outer shell of a word, so its first and last letters are lost

blocks.note: to be taken for a ride is to be deceived or led astray

explanation.surface: A man who has been conned after losing his court case.
explanation.walkthrough: MISLED without its outer letters gives ISLE. The Isle of Man is an island in the Irish Sea, so 'Man perhaps' defines by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is one example of an island, which is what an isle is.

clue.text: Beaten thus, I astounded boxing aficionado

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so the run of words holds the solution inside it

blocks.note: the letters run across beatEN THUS I ASTounded

explanation.surface: A boxing fan stunned to see a fighter beaten in such a way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxing' looks like the sport the fan follows, but it is the signal to look inside the words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: An aficionado is a keen devotee of some activity, which is exactly what an enthusiast is.

clue.text: You peeled and ate most exotic fruit

indicators.note: peeling strips off the skin, so the outside letters go and only the core remains
exotic suggests something strange and unfamiliar, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the middle letter of You
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: You peeled some exotic fruit and ate most of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exotic fruit' reads as one phrase, but exotic works on the letters before it and 'fruit' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanically the tomato is a fruit, the seed-bearing part of the plant, though cooked as a vegetable.

clue.text: Break wind, repelling leaders of Foreign Legion with greeting

indicators.note: leaders are those at the front, so only the initial letters are taken
repelling means driving away, so those letters are pushed out of the word
with means alongside, so the two pieces are simply put together

blocks.note: hi is a simple greeting
flatus is the medical word for intestinal wind
the first letters of Foreign and Legion

explanation.surface: A crude soldier's joke: a legionnaire breaking wind and greeting his commanders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break wind' is a phrase in the surface, but Break is the definition and wind is wordplay: flatus is the medical term for intestinal gas.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiatus is a pause or gap in a sequence, so it is a break in continuity.

clue.text: Type endowed with intelligence primarily?

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is wanted
one word is given another to hold, so it takes the letter inside itself

blocks.note: a genus is a class or kind, a type of thing
the first letter of intelligence

explanation.surface: Describes a person whose chief gift is a brilliant mind.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: it builds the word and also describes it, a type of person gifted with intellect above all.
explanation.definitionFit: A genius is someone of exceptional intellectual ability, a kind of person blessed mainly with brains.

clue.text: Ladder to keep impeding one's escape

indicators.note: something impeding gets in the way, so it is placed in the middle of the other word

blocks.note: a ladder in tights is a run
a keep is the stronghold of a castle, a fort
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A prisoner's escape ladder blocked from reaching the castle keep.
explanation.walkthrough: A ladder is British for a run in tights or stockings, and a keep is a castle's central tower.
explanation.definitionFit: To run for it is an idiom meaning to flee quickly, to make a dash and get away.

clue.text: Heard correspondence briefly describing short article in Time

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the final letter is dropped
short means lacking its end, so the last letter goes
to describe can mean to draw around, so one piece encircles the other

blocks.note: rhyme is a correspondence of sounds heard at the ends of words
the definite article

explanation.surface: Correspondence overheard describing a short article in Time magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: Time sounds like the magazine but is the musical sense. 'Heard correspondence' is a matching of sounds, as at line ends in verse.
explanation.definitionFit: In music time and rhythm both mean the regular pattern of beats underlying a piece.

clue.text: Cheating's "like, more grown-up" apparently!

blocks.note: a jokey comparative of adult
-y is a suffix meaning like or having the quality of, as in silky

explanation.surface: Someone excuses an affair as just being, like, more grown-up.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter treats the answer as a made-up adjective: ADULTER (more adult) plus the suffix Y, hence 'apparently'.
explanation.definitionFit: Adultery is sexual infidelity within marriage, the commonest sense of cheating on a partner.

clue.text: Conservative prime minister adopting Labour leader's constitution

indicators.note: the leader is at the front, so only the first letter is taken
adopting means taking in, so the letter is placed inside the other name

blocks.note: Edward Heath was Conservative Prime Minister 1970 to 1974
the first letter of Labour

explanation.surface: A Tory leader adopting the Labour leader's constitution, a political paradox.
explanation.walkthrough: HEATH takes in L: HEA(L)TH. Constitution looks political but here means physical makeup.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's constitution is their general physical condition, which is their state of health.

clue.text: Carers hope to change carpets

indicators.note: to change the words is to alter them, so their letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Care workers hope to replace a home's carpets.
explanation.walkthrough: Carpets reads as floor coverings, but here it is the verb: to carpet someone is to tell them off.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet is informal British for scolding, called on the carpet; reproaching is expressing disapproval of someone.

clue.text: Pouring rain stopping me finishing water colour

indicators.note: pouring suggests a tumbling flow, so those letters are jumbled
to stop something can mean to plug it, so these letters fill a gap inside
finishing means coming at the end, so this part follows the other

blocks.note: aqua is Latin for water
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Heavy rain stops me finishing a watercolour painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Water colour' suggests painting, but water is wordplay and colour alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquamarine is a pale blue-green shade named after the gemstone of that hue.

clue.text: Spectacled bears reduced to the last pair roughly

indicators.note: cut down to the final two letters, so only the end of that word survives

blocks.note: a pair of spectacles is drawn as two rings, and being spectacled means having them round the eyes, so they frame what follows
the last two letters of bears

explanation.surface: Spectacled bears, an endangered species, cut down to the last couple or so.
explanation.walkthrough: Spectacled bears are a real South American species. Here the word does double duty: the glasses supply two O's and also wear the other letters between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Or so is an idiom tacked onto a number meaning approximately, about that many.

clue.text: This may be decisive in turning drinker against drink

indicators.note: turning round makes the word run the other way

blocks.note: a sot is a habitual drunkard
to sup is to drink in small mouthfuls

explanation.surface: Turning a drinker against alcohol could be the decisive moment in recovery.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: a coin flip can settle who starts a contest, so it may decide things.
explanation.definitionFit: A toss-up is the flip of a coin used to decide something, or a situation whose outcome is even.

clue.text: Race is on to develop plan of action

indicators.note: developing means evolving into a new form, so these letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Pressure is on to draw up a strategy before a deadline.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is a postulated sequence of events, a projected outline of how things will play out.

clue.text: Sickness caused by new service for addicts tackling habit

indicators.note: to tackle is to grapple with something, wrapping round it

blocks.note: N is a standard abbreviation for new
Alcoholics Anonymous is a support service for people addicted to drink
use as in regular custom or practice, a habit

explanation.surface: Nausea brought on by a new rehab programme tackling a drug habit.
explanation.walkthrough: N, then AA wrapping USE: N + A(USE)A.
explanation.definitionFit: Nausea is a feeling of sickness in the stomach with an urge to vomit.

clue.text: Co-ordinate SAS basic training

indicators.note: training puts recruits through drills that reshape them, so the letters are reformed

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An order to co-ordinate basic training for the SAS, Britain's special forces.
explanation.walkthrough: Co-ordinate reads as a verb organising the training, but it is a noun from geometry.
explanation.definitionFit: The abscissa is the horizontal or x co-ordinate of a point on a graph.

clue.text: No longer bound after one has a change of heart

indicators.note: the heart is the middle of a word, so its central letters change places

blocks.note: people who are as one are united

explanation.surface: A couple are no longer bound together after one partner has a change of heart.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the middle I and T swap, turning UNITED into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Untied means unfastened or released, so something untied is no longer tied or bound up.

clue.text: Fashion's not out to make human condition better?

indicators.note: not here means without, so the following word is taken away

blocks.note: couture is high fashion design
taken as written

explanation.surface: A philosophical claim that fashion, never out of style, improves the human condition.
explanation.walkthrough: COUTURE minus OUT leaves C...URE. The question mark flags the playful definition: a human condition here is an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: To cure is to heal an illness, making a patient's medical condition better.

clue.text: Reveal surname periodically deleted on request

indicators.note: removing letters at regular intervals leaves every other letter behind

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of surname
to ask is to make a request

explanation.surface: A surname redacted from a document is disclosed when someone asks.
explanation.definitionFit: To unmask is to expose someone's true identity, so to reveal who or what they are.

clue.text: Economic policy of Margaret Thatcher initially exposed coal miners' suffering

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the opening letters are used
exposed means stripped of its covering, so the outside letters are removed
suffering suggests being in a bad way, so the letters are knocked into a new order

blocks.note: the initial letters of Margaret and Thatcher
the inner letters of coal
taken as written

explanation.surface: Thatcher's economic policy left coal miners suffering, as in the 1984-85 strike.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is apt: Thatcher's government pursued this policy and closed coal pits.
explanation.definitionFit: Monetarism is the economic theory of controlling inflation through the money supply, adopted by Thatcher's government.

clue.text: Note band leader's dropped in pitch

indicators.note: the leader is the front letter, and dropping it removes that letter

blocks.note: R.E.M. is an American rock band
as in pitch-dark, completely black

explanation.surface: A note that a band's leader has dropped out of tune.
explanation.walkthrough: Note and pitch suggest music, but pitch here means dark, as in pitch black.
explanation.definitionFit: A note can be a brief written or spoken comment, which is a remark.

clue.text: Reduce quality of broadcast following 1pm broadcast

indicators.note: following means coming after, so this piece is placed behind the other

blocks.note: the digit 1 is read as the letter I
to air something is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: A complaint that a programme's quality suffers when it follows the 1pm news.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'broadcast' scatters the letters of 1pm, with 1 read as I; the first gives AIR, which follows them.
explanation.definitionFit: To impair is to weaken or damage something, lowering its quality or strength.

clue.text: What might make one restless?

blocks.note: surface reading: something that makes a person fidgety or uneasy
setter's reading: restless taken literally as without rest, unable to sleep

explanation.walkthrough: Restless usually means agitated; read literally it means deprived of rest at night.
explanation.definitionFit: Insomnia is chronic inability to sleep, a condition that leaves a sufferer without rest.

clue.text: Bar raising large sum of money

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising lifts the word so it reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: pots of money means a great deal of it

explanation.surface: A bar raising a large sum for charity.
explanation.definitionFit: To bar something is to block or prevent it, which is to stop it.

clue.text: Set question almost provided written endorsement

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is left off

blocks.note: to ask is to question
to sign is to endorse something in writing

explanation.surface: An exam question set almost as soon as a signature endorsed it.
explanation.definitionFit: Set as in homework set by a teacher means allocated, which is what assigned means.

clue.text: This unpleasant person pursues public relations to make headway

indicators.note: pursuing means following behind, so the answer is what comes after that abbreviation in a longer word

blocks.note: to make headway is to make progress
PR is the usual abbreviation for public relations

explanation.surface: An unpleasant person chases good publicity to get ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer, placed after PR, would make the word for headway; take PR away to find it.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogress is a female ogre, a monstrous or cruel woman, so a very unpleasant person.
